key_concepts: Forces acting on an object can be represented using free-body diagrams
Net force is the vector sum of all forces acting on an object
Zero net force means balanced forces and no change in an object's state of motion
Nonzero net force changes an object's speed, direction, or both
Newton's first law states that objects resist changes in their state of motion
Friction is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces
The amount of friction depends on surface roughness and material
Reducing friction, such as with an air cushion, allows objects to move farther
Inertia explains why a resting object lags when its support is suddenly pushed
Inertia explains why a moving object continues forward when a vehicle suddenly stops
An object moving in a circle requires a centripetal force
Removing centripetal force makes an object move in a straight line tangent to the circle
